sara: heads-up — nightly long-context e2e for continuous-batching regressed on memory growth and tail latency. repro on llm-13b with kv_size=32GB. :warning:

sara: run log: 
```
2026-03-17T04:12:03Z serving: start workload longctx-accum
mem: resident 12.4G -> 28.7G over 45m
tail_p50 22ms p99 730ms -> p99 2.4s
kvcache_evictions: rising, contbatch_merge_coalesces: high
```

nate: can you paste the perf stack samples or flamegraph? is this deterministic?

sara: pretty consistent across 3 runs. flamegraph (top stacks):
```
cont_batch_merge                              31.6%
kv_reclaim_scan                                24.1%
kvslot_alloc_hotpath                            11.8%
dispatch_kernel_selector                        9.3%
gpu_driver_wait                                  6.2%
other                                            17.0%
```

dani: looks like the merge path spins up fragments from different ctx lengths and prevents kvslot reuse — head-of-line blocking when the head batch holds a fragment that can't be compacted. I reproduced with perf + eBPF sampling.

dani: pprof summary from the reproducible run:
```
Samples: 2000
#   Percent  Cumul.  Function
1    31.6%    31.6%  cont_batch::merge_batches
2    24.1%    55.7%  kv::reclaim_scan
3    11.8%    67.5%  kv::slot_alloc
4     9.3%    76.8%  runtime::kernel_selector
```

leo: hypothesis: the batch coalescer is merging across sequence-length buckets when prefix/KV hits differ, which increases fragmentation and forces reclaim to scan more pages. If a head batch has a long prefix, its fragments pin kvslots for long LRU windows => HOL for following short batches.

leo: quick mitigation patch idea: add a merge gating check that rejects merges if avg_prefix_tokens_ratio > 2.0 or if kv_fragmentation_score > 0.6. simple config flip to test: `merge_seq_tolerance=1.5` vs default 3.0.

frank: +1 to trying gating. also saw similar behavior when page-compact hysteresis was too aggressive — we compact immediately after reclaim which can thrash. raising compaction threshold reduced steady-state RSS in my repro.

frank: command to repro locally: 
```
./tools/bench_longctx --model llm-13b --mode continuous --kv-size 32G --batch-ttl 120s --prefetch-window 8
```

perf-bot: alert: nightly perf job #3245 failed regression threshold (mem_growth > 10GB). linked test: longctx-contbatch-llm13b. :alarm_clock:

nate: can someone attach the heapmap and a kvslot allocation timeline? would like to see which batch holds which slot over time.

sara: attaching short timeline excerpt (simplified):
```
00:00 batch A (len 4096) alloc slots [0..127] pinned
00:12 batch B (len 64) wants slots [0..31] -> waits
00:13 reclaim triggered -> scans pages 0..200, evicts tails but slot 0..127 pinned
00:40 mem climbs as B keeps waiting, more batches accumulate behind A
```

dani: that timeline nails the HOL behavior. merging B into A (merge_across_len) made the runtime treat them as single in-flight request and prevents reclaim because of cross-dependencies.

leo: proposed next steps:
- flip merge gating to conservative in staging (merge_seq_tolerance=1.2) and run longctx nightly
- add kvslot-level debug tracing for next 1000 requests (exposes which batch id pins which slot)
- plot eviction scans per minute vs merge_coalesce_rate

sara: created issue infra/eng-runtime#1482 and added logs + flamegraphs. tagging @nate @dani @leo for ownership.

nate: I'll land a short experiment: disable inter-length merges for continuous batching and run the perf harness overnight. if that fixes tail p99 and memory we can refine gating.

frank: if disable helps, follow-up is to make kernel_selector aware of prefix/kvcache locality — pick kernels that reduce KV pressure (shorter per-token cache retention or quantized kernel that reduces memory footprint).

dani: also adding a small optimization: when splitting merged batches, prefer splitting at fragment boundaries so we don't create additional tiny fragments that increase slab fragmentation.

leo: schedule a 30m debug sess tomorrow 10:30 PT to review results. :calendar:

sara: thanks all, tracking in the issue. will post results from the staging flip here. :thumbsup:
